A1.justification: Both PDFs describe UNCOMP. Their main texts, equations, figures, tables and appendices are readable and can be matched despite extensive rewriting and reorganization.

before.justification: v1 reports original LongBench, needle-in-a-haystack, compression, latency, throughput and ablation results in the main text and appendices.

after.justification: v2 retains original empirical evaluations and adds results on RULER, InfiniteBench and GSM8K, together with additional comparisons and analyses.

M1.justification: The two-stage compression framework remains, but v2 adds retrieval-layer identification and interpolation of that layer's parameters with the final layer, evaluated in Table 5. It also changes the stated covariance estimator from normalized centered token vectors to ordinary sample covariance. These substantially revise the documented entropy computation and inference procedure.

E1.justification: v2 retains LongBench and needle-in-a-haystack evaluation and adds RULER, InfiniteBench and GSM8K in Appendix E. These introduce multi-needle retrieval, tracing and aggregation scenarios, Chinese QA, additional mathematical and code tasks, and zero-shot/few-shot arithmetic reasoning. InfiniteBench's description alone does not establish that evaluation used contexts exceeding the model's input limit.

E2.justification: Table 1 adds StreamingLLM, Quest, Double-Sparse and RazorAttention to the retained H2O, SnapKV, PyramidKV and CHAI comparisons. The extreme-compression experiment newly compares CHAI and RazorAttention under head deletion. Appendix D.3 also adds an attention-variance grouping comparator; these are evaluated additions, not merely new citations.

E3.justification: The main experiment changes from two head groups with budgets 512/256 to eight groups starting at 640 with decrement 74. Appendix A revises entropy thresholds and layer-budget settings, and Qwen2.5-7B replaces Mistral. v2 removes the AMD latency comparison and introduces RULER evaluations at 4k/8k and GSM8K zero-, six- and twelve-shot protocols. These reported changes do not establish which experiments were rerun.

E4.justification: v2 adds entropy-versus-attention-variance comparisons at cache budgets 384 and 64, tests retrieval-layer interpolation, and expands full-versus-truncated rank and GQA head-pattern diagnostics. Earlier truncation and group-count ablations remain. The random and reversed-allocation controls are consolidated into Table 2, rather than being entirely new analyses.

E5.justification: v1 Section 4.2 explicitly says findings were confirmed by averaging multiple repeated experiments; v2 removes this statement. Neither version supplies explicit run counts, seeds, error bars or confidence intervals. This is a limited reporting change, with no evidence that the number of runs changed.

E6.justification: v2 adds substantial benchmark, comparator and retrieval-layer results and revises existing scores and timings. For example, Table 1's Llama3 Ours-group average changes from 40.21 to 40.52 under revised grouping settings, so this is not a demonstrated same-setting gain. CHAI's Llama3 needle score changes from 64.69 to 84.20. The reversed-allocation control changes from 5.89 to 13.86, while many earlier truncation, extreme-compression and throughput results remain unchanged.

T1.justification: v2 Eq. (1) substantively changes the covariance definition, removing the normalization that ensured trace one in v1. Appendix G extends Lemma 4 and its derivation with truncated-effective-rank bounds and cases depending on the truncation dimension, especially Eqs. (44)–(48). Most earlier proofs are retained and relocated, but the revised definition is not reconciled with their trace-one assumption.

C1.justification: v1 chiefly presents an efficient training-free compressor and GQA-style approach. v2 makes uncovering structured sparsity, identifying retrieval heads and layers, and connecting information compression to sparsity central contributions. Its introduction also adds an explicit priority claim for accelerating prefill through hidden-state compression. The principal cache-reduction and throughput claims remain.

C2.justification: v1 motivates deeper-layer pruning through increasing effective rank and richer token information. v2 emphasizes decreasing truncated rank as evidence of increasing sparsity, adds GQA-based explanations of shared head patterns, and proposes positional encoding as an explanation for query/key versus value/hidden-state differences. New limitations identify dense context-dependent tasks and information loss from miscalibrated uncertainty as concerns.

D1.justification: v2 adds a code-repository link, preparation-time information, and preparation/inference pseudocode in Appendix H, while revising checkpoint and hyperparameter documentation. It removes v1's explicit layer-group capacity schedules and cosine-similarity procedure for repairing outputs after head deletion. The new documentation is also inconsistent: Section 3.3.1 averages entropy values, whereas Algorithm 1 uses majority voting over group assignments.

R1.justification: v2 substantially repositions UNCOMP as an uncertainty-based explanation of hierarchical sparsity, extending v1's emphasis on training-free compression and head grouping. It adds substantive discussion of retrieval-head identification relative to DuoAttention and RazorAttention and incorporates research such as Quest, Double-Sparse and PyramidInfer. The dedicated head-compression survey is reorganized, and the bibliography expands considerably.

P1.justification: The title, abstract, introduction and substantial portions of the method and experimental discussion are rewritten. v2 organizes the method into preparation, layer-group and head-group stages with Observation, Discussion and Design passages. It reorders appendices, moves proofs, and adds limitations, risks and an algorithm walkthrough.

P2.justification: v2 adopts a two-column layout, substantially redraws the workflow, expands rank plots to compare full and truncated quantities, and adds head-pattern visualizations. Table 1 gains timing columns and comparator rows; grouping controls are consolidated, the GPU table loses its AMD block, and new benchmark tables and algorithm displays are added.

improvement.justification: The broader comparisons and task coverage, additional diagnostic analyses, code link and explicit limitations improve the evidence available to readers. However, v2 introduces central inconsistencies: Eq. (1) no longer ensures the trace-one normalization required by Appendix G, and Algorithm 2 reverses the entropy-change test in Eqs. (8)–(9). These leave the implemented estimator and compression rule unclear. The empirical benefits and theoretical/reproducibility harms do not support a reliable net quality judgment.
